introduction-the-builders-tools.core: The AWS CLI and SDKs (boto3, JavaScript, Go, Java…) call the same signed HTTPS APIs as the console. Automating with them makes work repeatable, scriptable and reviewable. Correct setup of credentials, profiles, regions and MFA is the foundation for safe automation.

first_principles.problem: Engineers click through the console for repetitive tasks and can't reproduce what they did.
truths: Every console action is an API call.

analogy.title: Power tools versus hand tools
analogy.story: Faster and repeatable, but you need to learn the safety switches.
analogy.breaks: Power tools are physical; leaked credentials can be misused from anywhere.

check.q: Why prefer CLI/SDK automation over console clicks?
check.a: It's repeatable, reviewable and scriptable, reducing human error.

initial-configuration-your-first-aws-con.core: aws configure sso (or aws configure for keys) writes ~/.aws/config (profiles, region, output, SSO settings) and ~/.aws/credentials (static keys, if used). Modern setups use IAM Identity Center: aws sso login obtains short-lived credentials cached locally, avoiding long-lived access keys entirely.

first_principles.problem: A developer pastes admin access keys into aws configure and they leak in a screenshot.
truths: Config and credentials files are separate.

analogy.title: A temporary visitor badge versus a permanent master key
analogy.story: The badge expires tonight; the key works until someone changes the locks.
analogy.breaks: Badges are visible; credential files can be copied silently, so protect your laptop too.

steps.label: Use
steps.detail: aws sso login --profile dev && aws sts get-caller-identity --profile dev

code.text:
[profile dev]
sso_session = corp
sso_account_id = 111122223333
sso_role_name = Developer
region = eu-west-1
output = json

[sso-session corp]
sso_start_url = https://corp.awsapps.com/start
sso_region = eu-west-1
sso_registration_scopes = sso:account:access

check.q: Which command shows who the CLI is authenticated as?

profiles-managing-multiple-aws-accounts.core: Named profiles in ~/.aws/config represent account/role/region combinations: SSO profiles, or role-chaining profiles (role_arn + source_profile) for cross-account assume-role. Select with --profile or AWS_PROFILE, and use clear naming (company-env-role) to avoid running commands in the wrong account.

first_principles.problem: An engineer deletes resources in production thinking they were in dev.
derivation: Set **AWS_PROFILE** per terminal; show it in your **prompt**.

analogy.title: Separate, clearly labelled keyrings
analogy.story: One for home, one for the office, one for the warehouse, so you don't open the wrong door.
analogy.breaks: Keys only open matching locks; credentials work in any account they're valid for, silently.

code.text:
[profile acme-prod-admin]
role_arn = arn:aws:iam::999988887777:role/BreakGlassAdmin
source_profile = acme-identity
mfa_serial = arn:aws:iam::111122223333:mfa/alice
region = eu-west-1

check.q: How do you make a profile assume a role in another account?
check.a: Set role_arn and source_profile (optionally mfa_serial) in the profile.

credential-provider-chain-the-hierarchy-.core: SDKs and the CLI search for credentials in order: explicit code/CLI options, environment variables (AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID…), web identity token (IRSA/OIDC), shared config and credentials files (profiles, SSO), container credentials (ECS task role) and instance metadata (EC2 role). The first source found wins, which explains many 'wrong identity' surprises.

first_principles.problem: A script uses old environment-variable keys instead of the intended role, and gets AccessDenied.

analogy.title: Checking pockets for keys in a fixed order
analogy.story: Jacket first, then trousers, then bag; you use the first keys you find, even if they're old.
analogy.breaks: You'd notice wrong keys; the SDK silently uses whatever it finds first.

steps.label: Finding
steps.detail: Old keys in env took precedence over the SSO profile.

code.text:
env | grep AWS_
unset AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY AWS_SESSION_TOKEN
aws sts get-caller-identity

check.q: Which takes precedence: environment variable credentials or a profile in ~/.aws/config?
check.a: Environment variables (unless a profile is explicitly specified in code or via --profile).

mfa-on-cli-the-access-denied-trap.core: If IAM policies require MFA (aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent), long-lived CLI keys get AccessDenied because their requests carry no MFA context. Solutions: use SSO (MFA at login), configure mfa_serial on an assume-role profile so the CLI prompts for a code, or call sts get-session-token with --serial-number and --token-code for temporary MFA credentials.

first_principles.problem: A user with MFA-enforced policies can use the console but gets AccessDenied on every CLI command.
truths: Temporary credentials can carry MFA context.
derivation: Cache sessions to avoid repeated prompts.

analogy.title: A secure building that needs a badge plus a PIN
analogy.story: Your badge alone works on the lobby door but not on secure floors until you enter the PIN.
analogy.breaks: PINs are typed each time; MFA sessions last for hours once established.

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: CLI requests now carry MFA context for 12 hours.

code.text:
aws sts get-session-token --serial-number arn:aws:iam::111122223333:mfa/alice --token-code 123456 --duration-seconds 43200
# export the returned AccessKeyId/SecretAccessKey/SessionToken

check.q: Why do MFA-required policies deny plain access-key CLI calls?
check.a: Requests signed with long-term keys don't include MFA authentication context.

boto3-session-management-writing-correct.core: In boto3, a Session holds credentials, region and configuration; clients and resources come from a session. Use explicit sessions per profile or role, create clients once and reuse them, configure retries and timeouts via botocore Config, and use paginators for list operations. Clients are thread-safe; sessions and resources aren't.

first_principles.problem: A script silently uses the wrong region, misses results past the first page and crashes under throttling.

analogy.title: A configured travel adapter
analogy.story: Set it once for the right country and voltage, then plug in all your devices.
analogy.breaks: Adapters don't page through results; you must use paginators.

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: Right account, all pages, resilient to throttling.

code.text:
import boto3
from botocore.config import Config
session = boto3.Session(profile_name='acme-dev', region_name='eu-west-1')
s3 = session.client('s3', config=Config(retries={'mode': 'adaptive', 'max_attempts': 10}, connect_timeout=5, read_timeout=30))
for page in s3.get_paginator('list_objects_v2').paginate(Bucket='logs', Prefix='2026/10/'):
    for obj in page.get('Contents', []):
        print(obj['Key'])

check.a: List APIs return results in pages; paginators automatically fetch all pages.
